stem: An engineer tells a client that a retaining wall design is unsafe. The client overrules the engineer and orders construction to proceed as drawn. Under the NCEES Model Rules, what must the engineer do?

options.text: Proceed, because the client carries the liability once informed
Notify the client and any other authority that may be appropriate
Quietly strengthen the design without telling the client
Resign from the project and say nothing further

eli5: Keeping people safe outranks keeping the client happy. If you are overruled and someone could get hurt, you have to tell someone who can stop it.
solution:
The first duty in the Model Rules is to the public. When an engineer's judgment is overruled in a way that endangers health, safety or welfare, the engineer must notify the client or employer and any other authority that may be appropriate.

Proceeding, working around the client in secret, or walking away silently all leave the hazard in place.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to the public

stem: A licensed engineer is asked to sign and seal drawings that were produced by another firm. She did not supervise or review the work. May she seal them?

options.text: Yes, if she is licensed in that state
Yes, if the other firm indemnifies her
No, because the work was not prepared under her responsible charge
No, unless the client approves in writing

eli5: A seal is a promise that says "I was in charge of this and I stand behind it." You cannot make that promise about work you did not direct.
solution:
The Model Rules allow a licensee to seal only work in their area of competence that was prepared under their responsible charge, meaning their direct control and personal supervision.

Being licensed in the state, being indemnified or having the client's approval does not change who was in charge of the work.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: signing and sealing; Model Law definition of responsible charge

stem: An engineer designing a pump station for a city is offered a paid consulting role by the pump supplier on the same project. When may the engineer accept both payments?

options.text: Never
When the supplier's fee is below a set dollar limit
When the circumstances are fully disclosed and all interested parties agree in writing
When the engineer judges that it will not affect the design

eli5: Being paid by two sides of the same deal is only fair if nobody is kept in the dark. Everyone involved has to know and say yes.
solution:
The Model Rules bar compensation from more than one party for services on the same project unless the circumstances are fully disclosed and agreed to in writing by all interested parties.

The engineer's own belief that the design will not be affected is not enough, and there is no dollar threshold.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients

stem: A professional engineer licensed in one state wants to offer engineering services in a second state. Which route does the NCEES Model Law provide for someone who already holds a license elsewhere?

options.text: Practice under the home-state license for up to one year
Licensure by comity
Retake the FE exam
Register as an engineer intern

eli5: A license only works in the state that issued it. The second state can recognize what you already earned instead of making you start over.
solution:
Licensure by comity lets a board license an engineer who holds a license from another jurisdiction with comparable requirements.

A home-state license does not carry over on its own, and the FE exam and intern status are steps before a first license.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Law: licensure by comity

stem: In a negligence claim, an engineer's work is judged against which standard?

options.text: A guarantee that the finished work is free of defects
The care and skill ordinarily used by competent engineers in similar circumstances
Whatever the client instructed
The lowest-cost design that meets code

eli5: Engineers are not expected to be perfect. They are expected to be as careful as a good engineer normally is.
solution:
The standard of care is what a reasonably prudent engineer would do in the same situation.

It is not a warranty of a perfect result, and following a client's instruction does not excuse careless work.

verify.basis: Common-law principle of professional negligence (standard of care for design professionals)

stem: Which type of insurance covers claims that an engineer's design errors caused a client financial loss?

options.text: General liability
Professional liability (errors and omissions)
Workers' compensation
Builder's risk

eli5: Different policies cover different kinds of trouble. Mistakes in professional advice have their own policy.
solution:
Professional liability insurance covers negligent acts, errors and omissions in professional services.

General liability covers bodily injury and property damage, workers' compensation covers employee injuries, and builder's risk covers the work while it is being built.

verify.basis: Standard insurance definitions used in construction and design contracts

stem: Which of the following is required for a contract to be enforceable?

options.text: Notarization of all signatures
Consideration exchanged by the parties
Approval by the state licensing board
A written document in every case

eli5: A contract is a trade. Each side has to give something of value, or it is only a promise.
solution:
A valid contract needs an offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties and a lawful purpose.

Many contracts are enforceable without being written or notarized.

verify.basis: Common-law elements of a valid contract

stem: An owner agrees to pay a contractor one fixed price for the whole job, whatever it actually costs the contractor. What type of contract is this?

options.text: Unit price
Cost plus fixed fee
Lump sum
Time and materials

eli5: With one fixed price, the builder keeps the savings if the job goes well and eats the loss if it does not.
solution:
A lump sum contract fixes the total price, so the contractor carries the cost risk.

Unit price pays per measured quantity. Cost plus and time and materials reimburse actual costs.

stem: A supplier offers an engineer a paid holiday if the engineer specifies the supplier's pumps on a client's project. Under the NCEES Model Rules, what should the engineer do?

options.text: Accept, provided the pumps meet the specification
Accept, then tell the client afterwards
Decline the offer
Accept only if the value is modest

eli5: A gift tied to a decision you make for a client is a bribe, whatever it is called.
solution:
The Model Rules forbid soliciting or accepting gratuities from contractors, suppliers or other parties in connection with work for an employer or client.

The quality of the product does not change that.

verify.basis: FE Reference Handbook 10.0.1, Ethics and Professional Practice, Model Rules of Professional Conduct: obligation to employers and clients
